reference.title: Scenario 2: Heading level hierarchy
reference.shortdesc: Consider a Markdown file with multiple heading levels.

section.p: Consider a Markdown file with multiple heading levels. All Headings in a Markdown file will be converted to separate topics except the last Heading level. For example, if the last Heading level in a file is Heading 4 (####), then all Headings 1-3 (#-###) will be converted to topics, subtopics, and sibling topics.

entry.codeblock: # Alarm Management Alarm Management provides tools for creating, monitoring, and managing alarms. ## Alarm Notifier Alarm Notifier controls how alarm notifications are delivered. ### Creating a New Alarm Notification #### Procedure To create a new alarm notification: 1. Click **Alarms**. 2. Click **Add Notification**. 3. Configure the notification settings. 4. Click **Save**. ### Editing an Alarm Notification #### Procedure To edit an existing notification: 1. Select the notification. 2. Modify the required settings. 3. Click **Save**. ## Alarm Types Alarm Types define the conditions that generate alarms. ### Creating an Alarm Type #### Procedure 1. Click **Alarm Types**. 2. Click **Add Alarm Type**. 3. Enter the alarm details. 4. Save the configuration.

section.p: Result: The converter creates a separate DITA topic for each Heading 1, Heading 2, and Heading 3 element in the Markdown file and establishes the parent-child hierarchy based on the heading levels. The Heading 1 topic (Alarm Management) becomes the parent topic, the Heading 2 topics (Alarm Notifier and Alarm Types) become child topics, and the Heading 3 topics become nested child topics under their respective Heading 2 parents.
section.note: Heading 4 ( #### ) is the deepest heading level used in this file. It becomes a p tag within the topic in the generated DITA hierarchy.
